solver.kind: blind AI solver B (separate agent, answer-free packet, adversarial rubric)

E069-01.notes: Plural antecedent 'they' (three structures) needs 'were'; B progressive and D present tense clash with past 'Built in the 1920s and 1930s'. Facts (Denge sound mirrors: ~61 m wall, two dishes, ~20-mile detection, superseded by radar late 1930s) check out.

E069-02.notes: 'knots' is countable, so 'fewer'. C uses amount-language for a count noun; D 'a fewer number of' is unidiomatic (would be 'a smaller number of').

flags.note: Notional agreement: 'A group of shop owners were worried' is widely accepted in edited prose (several usage guides allow a plural verb when the 'group of + plural noun' emphasizes individuals). ACT convention favors singular 'was', and B/C fail on tense, so D is still the single best answer, but a reviewer may want a less contestable collective head noun (e.g., 'The owner of the shops') or a subject with no 'of + plural' phrase.

E069-03.notes: Head noun 'group' is singular; past narrative requires 'was'. B (present perfect) and C (present progressive) break tense.

E069-04.notes: Object of 'thanked' in a compound: 'Delia and me'. C reflexive/intensive misuse; D subject pronoun.

E069-05.notes: Possessive 'its cargo'. D 'the ships cargo' lacks apostrophe and also would be plural-ship mismatch with 'A ship'. Ideal-X facts (April 1956, Newark to Houston, 58 containers, McLean) are accurate.

E069-06.notes: 'earlier' duplicates 'existed before his'; A, B, C all retain the redundancy (B doubly). D 'several other designs' is concise. Morgan facts (1923 patent, GE $40,000 reported sale, newspaper and hair-care businesses) are accurate as commonly reported.

E069-07.notes: Subject is singular 'flood' (prepositional phrase 'of requests from bakers' is intervening); 'was' matches past tense. D shifts tense. Unlike 'a number of', 'flood of' is not a standard notional-plural quantifier, so NO CHANGE is not defensible. Bundt/Tunnel of Fudge facts (1950 Hadassah, 1966 Bake-Off, second place, Ella Helfrich of Texas) are accurate.

E069-08.notes: Gerund subject 'manufacturing them' is singular -> 'was'; plural 'them' is the trap. B present tense and plural; D plural progressive. Latimer facts (Navy, Bell drawings 1876, 1882 filament patent, joined Edison 1884, Edison Pioneers, d. 1928) are accurate.

E069-09.notes: Possessive 'its pieces'; C 'its'' is never correct. Tetris facts (1984, Academy of Sciences computer center, text-only display, tetra+tennis, 1996 Tetris Company) are accurate.

E069-10.notes: Possessive relative 'whose curiosity'. C 'who is curiosity' is nonsense; D 'her' creates a comma splice inside the main clause. Kwolek facts (1965, tire-fiber search, reluctant technician, Kevlar early 1970s, Inventors Hall of Fame) are accurate.

E069-11.notes: 'Neither' is singular in formal written English -> 'attempts was'; 'attempts' must stay plural after 'of these'. B mismatches 'these attempt'; D present tense clashes with the past narrative. Informal 'neither ... were' would not be accepted by a careful ACT editor. Bubble Wrap facts (1957, Fielding & Chavannes, wallpaper, greenhouse insulation, Sealed Air 1960, IBM, last Monday in January) are accurate.

E069-12.notes: Singular 'Recognition' + past -> 'was'. Henson facts (1887 hat store, Nicaragua survey, April 6, 1909 with four Inuit, 1944 medal, 1988 Arlington reburial beside Peary) are accurate.

E069-13.notes: A: semicolon followed by a fragment. C: comma splice. D: colon followed by verbless fragment ('it remarkably well preserved'). B gives a relative clause with a verb. 2022 wreck depth ~3,008 m (~9,870 ft) makes 'nearly 10,000 feet' accurate; other Shackleton facts check out.

E069-14.notes: Past-tense historical narrative requires 'had to dismount'. A present perfect, B future perfect-ish, D 'must have dismount' is ungrammatical (needs participle). WPA packhorse library dates (1935-1943) accurate.

E069-15.notes: Compound subject 'The explosion and the fires' -> plural 'were'. C 'has been held responsible' is singular and changes meaning; B singular present progressive. Halifax facts (Dec 6, 1917, Mont-Blanc/Imo, ~9:04, ~2,000 deaths, Coleman, Boston relief and blizzard, annual tree since 1971) are accurate.

E069-16.notes: Design gets one short paragraph; essay pivots to Seneca Village and eminent domain. A misstates content (no tree selection detail); C overstates the sunken roads; D is contradicted by 'almost every hill and pond was designed.' Seneca Village figures (~225 residents, about two-thirds Black, over half of Black households owning land) match Central Park Conservancy accounts.
